grammar.title: Frase
grammar.rule: Recebi minha pasta. A pessoa devolveu a pasta. Consegui encontrar a página.
grammar.note_en:
This chapter extends the completed past, called pretérito perfeito, to encountered -er and -ir verbs. The completed event changes the evidence on the table: Recebi minha pasta means “I received my folder”; devolvi a pasta means “I gave the folder back.” Compare Paulo recebeu a pasta agora, “Paulo received the folder just now,” with agora tenho a pasta, “now I have the folder.” The first reports the completed transfer; the second gives the resulting possession. A finished action can occur earlier today, not only yesterday.

For the encountered regular -er verbs, remove -er and add -i with eu or -eu with a singular name or você. Receber gives recebi, “I received,” and recebeu, “he/she/you received.” Devolver gives devolvi, “I gave back,” and devolveu, “he/she/you gave back.” Entendi o caminho means “I understood the route.” The story uses this to show Bia reaching understanding after Paulo explains. These tables describe the cells actually read; they do not license unseen forms of every verb ending in those letters. The new words are also introduced through the situation: a folder returns to its owner; an explanation turns not knowing into knowing.

For encountered -ir verbs, eu also ends in -i, while the singular name form ends in -iu: consegui, “I managed,” and conseguiu, “he/she/you managed.” Consegui encontrar a página means “I managed to find the page.” It expresses successful achievement, not just ability or a wish. Compare quero encontrar, “I want to find,” with consegui encontrar, “I managed to find.” Ana’s success follows the search, permission and actual opening. Você conseguiu encontrar a página, Ana means “You managed to find the page, Ana”: você takes the same verb form as a singular name.

Decidi procurar os nomes means “I decided to look for the names.” Decidimos ler as duas versões juntos means “We decided to read the two versions together.” Discutimos as duas listas means “We discussed the two lists.” The -imos ending can look identical to the present. In Hoje discutimos o caminho da pasta, “Today we discussed the route of the folder,” the next sentence moves to the current activity: Agora estamos discutindo as duas listas, “Now we are discussing the two lists.” Read the account as a whole; hoje alone does not determine tense. A completed discussion of one subject can precede an ongoing discussion of another. No accent is added to distinguish those readings.

The chapter also continues earlier -ar completed forms. Tirei a página means “I removed the page”; coloquei a página na minha pasta means “I put the page in my folder.” Abri is the completed eu form of abrir: abri minha pasta means “I opened my folder.” The subject, tense and actual verb form belong together. Do not substitute an irregular past of ser, ir or fazer: those are outside this chapter. Present permito, “I allow,” and permite, “he/she allows; you allow,” establish permission before the folder is opened. Pode abrir means “You may open it” here; the permission comes from its owner. The notes do not turn every possible complement construction into a new productive pattern.

Pasta is a folder for papers, distinct from bolsa, a bag. Receber is receiving an object; devolver is giving it back to its owner. The two café folders were exchanged; Paulo’s own leaf was inside his own folder. A versão is one form of a list: the same intended reading evening has two lists with different names and dates. That is evidence to compare, not proof of theft or a forged document. The receipts establish visits and payments; Paulo’s new recollection identifies where he removed the page. The story does not make a receipt’s clock the moment of removal.

The dates printed on the old lists belong to earlier weeks. Their sábado, seis and sábado, treze are not the recent receipt’s Saturday six and today’s Saturday thirteen. Dates can recur across weeks; neither old list is the current fifteen-book shipment list. Who proposed what is still to be read in the next chapter. Fictional document dates do not give real café schedules or historic claims.
